title: Self-employed parents: October starts a pension exemption you must claim
summary: ENACTED, effective October 1, 2026: National Pension Category 1 parents raising a child under 1 can apply to stop paying eligible pension premiums regardless of income, while those months still count as fully paid for Basic Pension. Hidden fine print: both eligible parents can qualify, already-paid eligible months can be credited or refunded, and babies born before October may still have remaining eligible months.
why_it_matters: This is not an income-tested hardship exemption. For self-employed, freelance, farming, student or unemployed parents who are Category 1 insured, a missed application can mean paying ¥17,920 per eligible month in FY2026 that the new rules allow to be exempted without reducing future Basic Pension credit.

claims.text: The National Pension childcare premium-exemption system takes effect October 1, 2026 for Category 1 insured parents raising a child under age 1; there is no income requirement, and exempt months are treated as contribution-paid months for Basic Pension calculation.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service, MHLW and current municipal implementation guidance.

claims.text: Eligibility requires the Category 1 insured parent to maintain the relevant legal parent-child relationship and live at the same address as the child; both spouses can qualify if both are Category 1 insured. Category 2 employees/public servants and Category 3 dependent spouses are outside this specific scheme.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service eligibility and exclusions.

claims.text: For a biological father or adoptive parent, exemption can run from the month childcare begins through the month before the child's first birthday, up to 12 months. A biological mother with the existing maternity exemption generally receives 9 additional childcare-exemption months after that maternity-exemption period. Only months from October 1, 2026 onward qualify under the new childcare exemption.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service and MHLW period rules.

claims.text: Parents already raising a child before October 2026 can qualify for remaining eligible months if the child is still under 1. Japan Pension Service gives the example of a child born January 1, 2026: October through December 2026 are eligible, three months.

If eligible months were already paid, or were already under ordinary exemption, payment deferment or student special-payment treatment, filing for childcare exemption can replace that treatment; already-paid premiums are applied or refunded.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service states that previously paid eligible premiums will be credited or refunded.

claims.text: The standard National Pension premium is ¥17,920 per month in FY2026 and ¥18,290 per month in FY2027.
claims.basis: Current Japan Pension Service premium table.

claims.text: Using Japan Pension Service's January 1, 2026 transition example, three eligible months from October through December would avoid ¥53,760 of FY2026 standard premiums per qualifying Category 1 parent; if both parents independently qualify, the household total for those same three months would be ¥107,520.
claims.basis: 3 months × ¥17,920; doubled only for a household in which both parents independently meet Category 1 eligibility.

claims.text: Parents of babies born earlier in 2026 face the greatest near-term risk of missing value because their transition window may contain only a few eligible months before the child's first birthday.
claims.basis: The transition rule ends eligibility at the month before the first birthday and does not backdate the new scheme before October 2026.

content.policy_status: ENACTED — effective October 1, 2026. Japan Pension Service's September 3 implementation bulletin explicitly lists the system as taking effect on that date.
content.key_message: Kung Category 1 National Pension parent ka at may baby na under 1, check this before October: the new exemption is not income-tested, but it requires a claim and the transition window can close quickly.
what_changed: From October 1, 2026, qualifying National Pension Category 1 parents can have eligible childcare months exempted from the monthly premium without losing Basic Pension credit.
Both qualifying Category 1 parents can use the scheme for the same child; it is not limited to the mother and there is no income test.
A child born before the launch date can still create entitlement for remaining months after October, but nothing before October is covered by the new childcare exemption.
Already-paid eligible premiums are not automatically wasted: Japan Pension Service says they can be applied or refunded after the childcare-exemption filing.
content.who_is_affected: National Pension Category 1 insured people age 20–59, such as many self-employed people, freelancers, farmers, students and unemployed people, who are biological or adoptive parents and are raising a child under age 1 while maintaining the required parent-child relationship and same address. This specific scheme does not apply to Category 2 employees/public servants covered by Employees' Pension or to Category 3 dependent spouses.
content.when: Effective October 1, 2026. Only eligible months on or after that date count. For biological fathers and adoptive parents, the period can run through the month before the first birthday, up to 12 months. For biological mothers who have the maternity premium exemption, the new childcare portion generally follows it for 9 months. Transitional babies already born before October can qualify only for the remaining eligible months.
content.financial_impact: The standard National Pension premium is ¥17,920/month in FY2026 and ¥18,290/month in FY2027. Actual household savings depend on the child's birth/adoption timing, which parent is Category 1, whether both parents qualify, and whether some months fall in the mother's maternity-exemption period. Exempt childcare months still count as paid for Basic Pension amount calculation.
content.risk_if_ignored: You may keep paying premiums for months that could have been exempted, or miss a short transition window before the child turns 1. Already-paid eligible months can be corrected, but that still requires the proper filing rather than assuming the system is automatic.
content.deadline: There is no single nationwide filing deadline stated on the central special page. The practical boundary is the eligibility period itself: the new exemption applies only from October 1, 2026 and generally ends at the month before the child's first birthday. Parents of children already born should verify eligibility now rather than waiting until after the child turns 1.
content.potential_benefit: Avoid monthly National Pension premiums during eligible childcare months while retaining full Basic Pension credit for those months; already-paid qualifying premiums can be credited or refunded.
content.downside: This is not a cash grant and does not cover everyone with a baby. Salaried employees/public servants and Category 3 dependent spouses are handled under different social-insurance rules, and the biological mother's new childcare-exemption period is generally 9 months after the existing maternity exemption rather than a new 12-month exemption.
content.common_mistake: Assuming the benefit is income-tested, mother-only, automatic, or unavailable because the premium was already paid. Japan Pension Service says none of those assumptions is generally correct for an otherwise eligible Category 1 parent.

do_now_vs_wait.do_now: Confirm your National Pension category, child's birth/adoption date, whether you live at the same address, and which months remain before the first birthday. If you have prepaid premiums, keep the payment record rather than assuming you are excluded.
do_now_vs_wait.wait: Do not simply stop paying before the exemption is properly reflected. Use the official Japan Pension Service/municipal procedure for the eligible period and keep confirmation of the filing.

fact_vs_inference.fact: The October 1 start, Category 1 scope, no-income-test rule, full pension credit, both-parent eligibility, transition months and refund/credit treatment are stated by Japan Pension Service/MHLW.
fact_vs_inference.inference: The story is especially time-sensitive for parents whose child will turn 1 soon after October because their usable transition period is short.

content.strongest_counterinterpretation: The headline benefit sounds broader than it is. Most company employees are not moved into this new scheme; they already have separate Employees' Pension/health-insurance maternity and childcare-leave premium exemptions. Category 3 spouses also do not directly pay National Pension premiums. So the new household saving is concentrated among Category 1 parents rather than all new parents in Japan.
content.what_remains_uncertain: Individual processing time and local counter workflow can vary. The central rules establish eligibility and the financial treatment, but readers should use the current Japan Pension Service or municipality procedure when filing, especially if their family situation involves different addresses, special adoption/foster arrangements, a recent insurance-category change or overlapping maternity exemption.
content.what_would_change_mind: ALAM should revise this recommendation if Japan Pension Service/MHLW delays the October 1 effective date, changes the Category 1/co-residence requirements, materially changes the treatment of already-paid premiums, or publishes later procedural guidance that changes how transitional claims must be filed.

reading_levels.30 sec: What happened: from Oct. 1, Category 1 National Pension parents with a child under 1 can claim premium-free eligible months with full pension credit. Why it matters: walang income test, both eligible parents can qualify, and already-paid eligible months can be refunded/credited. What to do: check your pension category and baby's first birthday now, especially if the baby was born before October. Bottom line: this is claim-based, not something to assume will happen automatically.
reading_levels.2 min: Japan is adding a childcare premium exemption specifically for National Pension Category 1 parents from October 1, 2026. The key difference from ordinary hardship exemptions is that income does not matter and the exempt months count as fully paid for future Basic Pension. Both qualifying parents can use it. The transition rule is especially valuable for 2026 births: a January 1 baby, for example, leaves three qualifying months—October to December—before turning 1. At the FY2026 rate that is ¥53,760 per qualifying parent. Company employees and Category 3 spouses are outside this specific scheme because different social-insurance rules apply to them.

outcomes: Identify whether you are in the National Pension category this new exemption actually covers.
Work out which childcare months can qualify, including a baby born before October 2026.
Understand why the exemption does not reduce Basic Pension credit and why already-paid eligible months can still matter.
learning.background: Japan's National Pension has different insured categories. Category 1 generally includes people who are not covered through an employer's Employees' Pension and are not a dependent Category 3 spouse—for example many self-employed people, freelancers, students and unemployed people. Until this reform, Category 1 parents did not have a broad income-free childcare premium exemption comparable to the premium relief tied to maternity/childcare leave in employee social insurance. The new system fills part of that gap from October 2026.

terms.term: 国民年金第1号被保険者 / Category 1 insured
terms.meaning: A National Pension category that commonly covers self-employed people, freelancers, farmers, students and unemployed people age 20–59 who are not insured as employees or dependent spouses.
terms.why_it_matters: The October childcare exemption is specifically aimed at this category.

terms.meaning: The new childcare-period exemption from National Pension premiums for eligible Category 1 parents raising a child under 1.
terms.why_it_matters: Unlike a normal unpaid period, these exempt months are treated as if the standard premium was paid when calculating Basic Pension.

how_it_works.title: First check the insurance category
how_it_works.explanation: Being a parent is not enough. The person claiming this specific exemption must be Category 1 insured during the eligible period and meet the parent-child and same-address conditions. Employees/public servants use a separate employee-insurance route, while Category 3 spouses have no direct National Pension premium to exempt under this scheme.

how_it_works.title: Then map the child's age to calendar months
how_it_works.explanation: The new system cannot create exempt months before October 1, 2026. A father or adoptive parent can generally receive months from when childcare begins through the month before age 1, up to 12 months. A biological mother's new childcare portion generally follows her existing maternity exemption for 9 months.

how_it_works.title: Filing changes the premium treatment, not the pension credit
how_it_works.explanation: Once an eligible month is treated as a childcare-exemption month, the standard National Pension premium is not owed for that month but the month still counts as contribution-paid for Basic Pension calculation. If the premium was already paid, Japan Pension Service says it can be applied or refunded.

learning.example: Japan Pension Service's own transition example uses a child born January 1, 2026. The new scheme cannot cover January–September, but October, November and December 2026 are eligible before the first birthday. At ¥17,920/month, that equals ¥53,760 per qualifying Category 1 parent. If both parents independently meet Category 1 eligibility, the same three-month household amount would be ¥107,520.
takeaways: Effective date is October 1, 2026—not retroactive to earlier 2026 months.
There is no income test for an otherwise eligible Category 1 parent.
Both qualifying parents can claim for the same child.
Eligible exempt months still count as fully paid for Basic Pension.
Already-paid eligible premiums can still be corrected through the official filing.

action_plan.goal: Identify every eligible childcare month and make sure it is treated under the new premium exemption rather than unnecessarily paid as a normal National Pension month.
action_plan.who_should_act: Parents who are or expect to be National Pension Category 1 insured on or after October 1, 2026 while raising a child under age 1. Company employees/public servants and Category 3 dependent spouses should use their applicable employee/dependent rules instead of this checklist.
action_plan.deadline: Prepare before October 1 if possible. No single national application deadline is stated on the central special page, but the entitlement window generally ends at the month before the child's first birthday, so parents of babies already born in 2026 should check promptly.
prepare: Your current National Pension insurance category or pension enrollment information.
The child's birth/adoption date and current address relationship.
Records of any National Pension premiums already paid or prepaid for months from October 2026 onward.
Access to official Japan Pension Service/municipal pension procedures when you are ready to file.

steps.step: Confirm you are in the right pension category
steps.action: Verify that you are Category 1 insured during the months you want exempted.
steps.how: Check your Japan Pension Service/Nenkin Net records or confirm with the municipality/Japan Pension Service if your status recently changed because of employment, resignation or dependency.
steps.done_when: You know whether you are Category 1, Category 2 or Category 3 for the relevant months.

steps.action: Write down October 2026 onward and stop at the applicable end of the childcare-exemption period.
steps.how: Use the child's birth/adoption timing and Japan Pension Service's rules. For a baby already born before October, include only months from October onward that remain eligible before age 1.
steps.done_when: You have a specific list of calendar months you believe should be exempt.

steps.action: Compare the eligible-month list with bank, card, payment-slip or prepayment records.
steps.how: Do not exclude a month merely because it was already paid. Japan Pension Service says paid eligible premiums can be applied or refunded after the childcare-exemption filing.
steps.done_when: You know which eligible months are unpaid, paid or prepaid.

steps.action: Submit the childcare-exemption notification using the current Japan Pension Service/municipal procedure for your eligible period.
steps.how: Use Japan Pension Service's official childcare-exemption page and the municipality's National Pension counter/procedure rather than an unofficial intermediary. Follow the current filing instructions because local handling details may differ.
needed: Any documents the official procedure specifically requests
steps.done_when: You have official submission/receipt confirmation or the municipality/Japan Pension Service confirms the filing has been accepted.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming high household income disqualifies you; this exemption has no income test.
Assuming only the mother can claim; both Category 1 parents can qualify.
Assuming a 2026 birth before October is automatically too early; remaining eligible months can still qualify.
Assuming a prepaid month cannot be corrected; Japan Pension Service explicitly provides for credit/refund of paid eligible premiums.
Stopping payment on your own without completing the official exemption procedure.
Using this Category 1 scheme if you are actually an Employees' Pension-insured worker or Category 3 dependent spouse.

decision_rules.if: You are Category 1, live with the child, and the child will still be under 1 during one or more months from October 2026 onward
decision_rules.then: Prepare and file for the eligible childcare-exemption months.

decision_rules.if: Both parents are independently Category 1 and meet the child/address requirements
decision_rules.then: Check eligibility for each parent separately; Japan Pension Service says both can be covered.

decision_rules.if: You already paid or prepaid an eligible month
decision_rules.then: Still file; the official rules provide for crediting or refunding paid eligible premiums.
Do not use this specific Category 1 exemption; check the separate employee/dependent social-insurance rules.

action_plan.follow_up: After filing, confirm that the eligible months are recorded as childcare-exemption months and check any refund/credit handling for premiums already paid. Re-check if your employment status, address with the child or pension category changes during the period.
